key_insight: Spherical propeller forcing produces a purely forward energy cascade across scale space, even though energy flux retains directional dependence in nearly homogeneous isotropic turbulence.
engineering_relevance: The findings support the design and characterization of turbulence-generation chambers by linking forcing geometry and propeller frequency to turbulent energy dynamics.
method: Apply the Kármán–Howarth–Monin framework to scale-by-scale energy transfer without assuming isotropy.
Measure Eulerian temporal statistics under low mean flow, where Taylor’s frozen-turbulence hypothesis does not apply.
Develop a propeller-frequency scaling framework using current measurements and previously reported HIT chamber data.
evidence_signal: Experiments show orientation-averaged structure functions consistent with Kolmogorov’s two-thirds law and intermediate-scale frequency statistics supporting Tennekes’ Eulerian spectrum.
watch_item: Nearly isotropic energy distributions do not guarantee isotropic energy flux, which remains sensitive to residual forcing asymmetries.
paper_title: Interscale energy transfer in a propeller-driven homogeneous and isotropic turbulence generation device
